solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Savage half of African secret society line

indicators.note: only half of the society's doubled name is wanted, the front portion

parts.note: the Mau Mau were a secret movement in 1950s Kenya

explanation.surface: A violent attack attributed to a member of a secret society, with a line of text describing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes MAU from MAU MAU, the Kenyan secret movement of the 1950s uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: To savage is to attack fiercely and tear at, as a mauling animal does.

clue.text: Pertinent to vessels is shape of orbit when captured by planet

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Venus is the second planet from the Sun
a ring or circular orbit is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An astronomy note: an orbit's shape when a satellite is caught by a planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when captured by' puts O, the round outline of an orbit, inside VENUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Venous is an adjective meaning relating to veins, which are blood vessels.

clue.text: Skilful Dutch earthenware's not large

indicators.note: saying the earthenware is not large means the size letter must be dropped from it

parts.note: Delft is the tin-glazed pottery named after the Dutch town
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A skilled potter's Dutch earthenware is modest in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes L, for large, from DELFT, the blue-and-white Dutch pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft is a synonym of skilful: neat and quick with the hands.

clue.text: Old Style goddess of rainbows, chief Egyptian deity

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for Old Style, the Julian calendar dating
Iris was the Greek goddess personifying the rainbow

explanation.surface: A list of old-fashioned deities: a rainbow goddess and the head of the Egyptian pantheon.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was god of the dead and the afterlife, among the most important gods of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Intriguing images involving unusual toil

indicators.note: to involve here is to enfold, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: pics is informal shorthand for pictures or images

indicators.note: unusual signals that the word toil is rearranged

explanation.surface: Fascinating pictures featuring people at strange labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' and 'involving' are the signals. 'Intriguing' looks like an adjective, but here it is the noun for scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: Intriguing as a noun means plotting and scheming, which is what office or party politics involves.

clue.text: City division set up grassed area, one ringed by lines about Brandenburg's opening

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the assembled pieces are read upwards
ringed by means enclosed, so the two lines go round the other pieces

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so two of them are LL
a lawn is a grassed area of a garden
I is the Roman numeral for one
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A garden scene: a lawn laid out and ringed by lines near the Brandenburg Gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringed by' encloses both grassed area and one; 'set up' reads LLAWNILREB upwards, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berlin Wall divided the city of Berlin between East and West from 1961 to 1989.

clue.text: No oil painting needs fine pair of experts to grip hearts

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: to grip is to hold within, so the hearts letter sits inside the pair
a pair means the word is used twice

parts.note: an ace is an expert
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A poor painting needs two skilled restorers to put some heart into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of' gives ACEACE, and 'to grip' puts H inside the second ACE. Facache is British slang for an ugly or miserable-looking person.
explanation.definitionFit: No oil painting is a British idiom for unattractive; a face-ache is an ugly or sour-faced person.

clue.text: Codger grabbing the woman's cigar

indicators.note: grabbing means holding onto, so one piece is clutched inside the other

parts.note: an old coot is a silly old man, like a codger
her is the possessive meaning belonging to the woman

explanation.surface: An old man snatches a woman's cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' is the container signal; an old coot is slang for a foolish old man.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a type of cigar with both ends cut square.

clue.text: Disreputable bunch who'll turn up

definitions.meaning: British slang for a useless or worthless group of people
one who shows, that is, someone who appears

explanation.surface: A dodgy crowd who are bound to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as show plus -er: someone who shows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a group a right shower is British slang for a contemptible lot; literally it also means one who shows.

clue.text: An affair absorbing Conservative in recess

parts.note: an becomes the indefinite article A

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a love affair, shortened to love

explanation.surface: A political affair involving a Tory conducted in a hidden corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts C inside LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess in the wall of a room.

clue.text: Towelling robes in the same place, left in a bad way

indicators.note: to robe is to clothe, so the outer piece wraps round the inner ones

parts.note: terry is looped towelling fabric
ib is short for ibidem, meaning in the same place

explanation.surface: Towelling robes abandoned in one spot, looking shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'robes' looks like a noun but is a verb: TERRY clothes IB and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Terribly is an adverb meaning badly or very poorly, matching the phrase describing a bad manner.

clue.text: British sailor's hint of being in proper order?

definitions.text: British sailor's hint of being in proper order?

indicators.note: the words are being put into their proper order, so they are currently jumbled and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A British seaman's sign that everything is shipshape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in proper order' rearranges SAILORSHINTOF after B. The whole clue also describes the phrase: sailors' praise for the efficient port of Bristol, as in 'shipshape and Bristol fashion'.
explanation.definitionFit: The expression means neat and in good order, originally said of ships in a well-run harbour.

clue.text: Rickety truck, bus and (Continental) car barely held together?

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the words are jumbled

parts.note: et is French, a Continental language, for and

explanation.surface: A list of ramshackle vehicles: a truck, a bus and a foreign car about to fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rickety' signals the jumble; the bracketed 'Continental' says the word for and is French.
explanation.definitionFit: A rust bucket is an informal term for an old, badly corroded vehicle that barely holds together.

clue.text: Sin of Devil-dealer giving up soul at the outset for start in life

indicators.note: giving up one thing for another means swapping it out for a replacement

parts.note: Faust is the legendary scholar who made a pact with the Devil

indicators.note: at the outset means the first letter of the word
start in means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The sin of a man who sold his soul at the start of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up' and 'for' swap S, the first letter of 'soul', for L, the first of 'life', in FAUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A fault is a moral failing or misdeed, a mild synonym of sin.

clue.text: Recessive feature of Lemuel's in Lilliput, say

indicators.note: recessive suggests going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
a feature of the words is something contained within them

explanation.surface: A genetics remark about a trait Lemuel inherited, set in Lilliput.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature of' finds ELSI inside 'Lemuel's in', and 'Recessive' reverses it. Lemuel Gulliver visits Lilliput in Swift's Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilliput is the fictional island in Gulliver's Travels, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: Number 101 in my view, flipping moody image

indicators.note: flipping turns the pieces over, so the whole run is read upwards

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals
to me means in my opinion

explanation.surface: Room 101 in my opinion: a grimly moody picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses NO + CI + TO ME. 'flipping' also reads as a mild British expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley or frowning face in text is a little picture that shows the writer's mood.

clue.text: Eclipse mostly loyal politician

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: true means faithful or loyal
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Mostly outshining a faithful politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump is to outdo or surpass, as to eclipse someone is to overshadow them.

clue.text: Slap concertina

definitions.meaning: theatrical slang for stage make-up, applied heavily
to collapse or crumple flat, as vehicles in a crash or floors of a building

explanation.surface: Hitting an accordion-like instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slap' is actors' slang for greasepaint, and pancake is a heavy flat make-up; a structure that concertinas collapses flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancake is a thick make-up, theatrical slap; as a verb it means collapse flat, like a concertina folding.

clue.text: Son with seaman making deck cleaner

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A father and his sailor son swabbing the deck together.
explanation.definitionFit: A swab is a mop used for cleaning a ship's deck.

clue.text: Change opinions, hit with a pair of taps?

parts.note: a blow is a hit
a sink usually has two taps, one marked hot and one cold

explanation.surface: Changing your mind, then hitting someone with a pair of taps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taps' are faucets, not light blows.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow hot and cold is an idiom for keep changing one's mind or attitude.

clue.text: Enthusiastic judge, judge waiving right for outdoorsy type

parts.note: to hear a case is to judge it in court

indicators.note: waiving means giving up, so the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: An eager judge sets aside a right for an outdoor sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiving' drops R from TRY. The word also means a sporty outdoors type, so 'for outdoorsy type' supports the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty means warm and vigorous, as an enthusiastic welcome is.

clue.text: Form a solid mass in ringlets, perhaps, raising daughter

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising moves the letter higher up the word

parts.note: ringlets are an example of curled hair

explanation.surface: Hair in ringlets, perhaps from bringing up a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' lifts D two places up CURLED. 'raising' looks like bringing up a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk curdles when it separates into thick lumps, so to curdle is to clot into a solid mass.

clue.text: To start penultimate section of Macbeth, for example, was worrying

parts.words: penultimate section of Macbeth, for example
parts.note: Shakespeare's plays have five acts, so the penultimate one is act four, written Act IV
ate, as in what was eating him, means was troubling him

explanation.surface: Starting the fourth act of Macbeth was nerve-racking.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth, like Shakespeare's other plays, has five acts.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate a machine is to set it going or start it.

clue.text: Last of five regular instalments of quartos for 100 cents

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word five
regular instalments means every other letter of the word quartos

explanation.surface: Five regular payments made for some quarto books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular instalments of' takes the even letters of 'quartos'.
explanation.definitionFit: The single European currency unit is divided into a hundred cents.

clue.text: Commercial rent out of control?

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a commercial
a rent is a split or tear, as is a rift

explanation.surface: A commercial lease that has run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like the payment for property, but here it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat adrift floats freely without steering, so it is out of anyone's control.

clue.text: Playful king's soulful music

parts.note: fun as an adjective means playful or amusing
K is the chess abbreviation for king, with the possessive acting as a link

explanation.surface: A light-hearted king enjoying some soul music.
explanation.definitionFit: Funk is a rhythmic genre of African American dance music grown out of soul.

clue.text: Turned to the other side, lieutenant in mutiny

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: over means across, to the other side

explanation.surface: A lieutenant changes sides during a mutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses OVER. The surface suggests defecting, which hints at the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolt is a rebellion or uprising, as a mutiny is aboard ship.

clue.text: A white lining for vest that's irritating to wear

indicators.note: to wear something is to have it on, so the irritating word has the lining inside it

parts.note: riling means annoying or irritating

indicators.note: the lining of a word is its inner letters, between the ends

explanation.surface: A white lining for a vest that is itchy to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lining for' and 'to wear' are the signals. 'A white' means a white wine, not a white garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a grape variety used for a well-known white wine.
